## Figure 1.9: Average Terms on New External Debt Commitments for Low- and Middle-Income Countries, by Creditor Type, 2015–25
Line chart with two panels.

- **Panels**
  - **a. Private creditors**
  - **b. Official creditors**
- **Time span:** 2015–2025
- **Geography/group:** Low- and middle-income countries
- **Series/legend**
  - **Grace period**
  - **Maturity**
  - **Interest (right axis)**
- **Left axis:** **Grace period and maturity (years)**, range **0 to 40**
- **Right axis:** **Percent**, range **0 to 7**

### Panel a. Private creditors
Approximate values read from line positions:

| Year | Grace period (years) | Maturity (years) | Interest, right axis (%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2015 | ≈10.2 | ≈12.1 | ≈4.1 |
| 2016 | ≈8.1 | ≈13.8 | ≈5.4 |
| 2017 | ≈11.0 | ≈15.4 | ≈4.6 |
| 2018 | ≈8.7 | ≈10.8 | ≈5.2 |
| 2019 | ≈12.5 | ≈15.5 | ≈5.2 |
| 2020 | ≈13.4 | ≈14.4 | ≈4.3 |
| 2021 | ≈13.4 | ≈14.5 | ≈4.2 |
| 2022 | ≈5.6 | ≈10.1 | ≈4.3 |
| 2023 | ≈7.9 | ≈13.0 | ≈6.0 |
| 2024 | ≈7.4 | ≈12.5 | ≈5.9 |
| 2025 | ≈6.2 | ≈12.4 | ≈5.7 |

**Visual takeaways**
- For **private creditors**, **interest rates** are highest in **2023–24** at about **6%**, easing slightly in **2025** to about **5.7%**.
- **Maturity** is highest around **2017** and **2019** (about **15.5 years**) and lowest in **2022** (about **10 years**).
- **Grace period** drops sharply in **2022** to its lowest level (about **5.6 years**), then partially recovers but remains below pre-2022 levels through **2025**.
- In every year, **maturity exceeds grace period**.

### Panel b. Official creditors
Approximate values read from line positions:

| Year | Grace period (years) | Maturity (years) | Interest, right axis (%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2015 | ≈7.0 | ≈23.8 | ≈2.0 |
| 2016 | ≈6.0 | ≈21.5 | ≈2.0 |
| 2017 | ≈5.5 | ≈21.5 | ≈2.1 |
| 2018 | ≈5.7 | ≈22.1 | ≈2.5 |
| 2019 | ≈5.3 | ≈21.6 | ≈2.3 |
| 2020 | ≈5.4 | ≈21.1 | ≈1.5 |
| 2021 | ≈5.0 | ≈20.2 | ≈1.5 |
| 2022 | ≈5.7 | ≈20.9 | ≈2.0 |
| 2023 | ≈6.1 | ≈23.4 | ≈3.6 |
| 2024 | ≈6.0 | ≈24.2 | ≈3.3 |
| 2025 | ≈5.9 | ≈24.6 | ≈3.0 |

**Visual takeaways**
- For **official creditors**, **interest rates** are consistently below those of private creditors in every year shown.
- Official-creditor **interest** is lowest around **2020–21** (about **1.5%**) and peaks in **2023** (about **3.6%**) before declining to about **3.0%** in **2025**.
- **Maturity** remains much longer than for private creditors throughout, hovering around **20–25 years**, with the highest level in **2025**.
- **Grace period** is relatively stable, near **5–7 years**, with a mild uptick in **2022–24**.
- In every year, **official-creditor maturity** is substantially longer than **private-creditor maturity**.

### Cross-panel comparisons
- **Private-creditor interest rates** are visibly higher than **official-creditor interest rates** throughout **2015–25**.
- **Official creditors** offer much longer **maturities** than **private creditors** in all years.
- **Private-creditor grace periods** are generally somewhat longer than **official-creditor grace periods** before 2022, but they fall sharply in **2022** and narrow the gap thereafter.
- In **2025**, the chart shows roughly:
  - **Private creditors:** grace period ≈ **6.2 years**, maturity ≈ **12.4 years**, interest ≈ **5.7%**
  - **Official creditors:** grace period ≈ **5.9 years**, maturity ≈ **24.6 years**, interest ≈ **3.0%**

**Source:** World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
